static_traits.name: Su Kailin
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior counseling or treatment history; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, Positive attitude; able to describe trigger situations and automatic thoughts specifically; has catastrophizing and 'predicting the future' cognitive patterns; speech rate and pronunciation features Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: When volunteering at a nursing home, has intense fear about lifting or assisting the elderly, believing they will drop the elderly person and cause injury to others, and thus avoids related tasks.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to reduce Fear and Anxiety through counseling, recovering effectiveness and confidence in nursing-home volunteer service.
growth_experiences: Several months ago witnessed a resident fall at the nursing home; the client became highly tense from a strong sense of safety responsibility; since then Significant anxiety (racing heart, sweating) appears when lifting or assisting the elderly, gradually avoiding related tasks, seeking others to take over or asking colleagues for comfort and reassurance.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough and may hurt others
Ensuring others' safety is entirely my responsibility

special_situations.event: Specific lifting situations such as transferring an elderly person from wheelchair to bed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a small error occurs during the transfer, it will cause serious injury, and I will bear full responsibility
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Asking colleagues to take over, avoiding lifting/transfer tasks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will drop her; the consequences will be severe

special_situations.event: When encountering any task in the nursing home that requires lifting or assisting an elderly person
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Whenever someone needs to be lifted, I am very likely to slip and cause an accident
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids related tasks in advance; repeatedly seeks comfort and confirmation from colleagues before starting
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will definitely go wrong this time

special_situations.event: Recalls witnessing a resident fall a few months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Since that fall happened once, it can easily happen to me again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying hypervigilant and avoiding lifting situations as much as possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Falls like this will happen again on my watch

special_situations.event: Realizing my training is not as good as some medical staff, feeling uneasy about my abilities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not had enough training, I should not take on lifting, otherwise I will definitely make mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-limiting: only participating when more skilled personnel are present, or directly handing it over to them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not lift them; professionals must do it

core_conflict.wish: Longs to ensure others' safety and to be seen as a reliable and trustworthy helper
core_conflict.fear: Fears his own mistakes causing others to be injured and being blamed; experiences strong self-blame
defense_goal: Reducing risk and Anxiety by avoiding lifting tasks and letting others take over

object_relations.self_representation: An inadequately trained volunteer prone to mistakes who needs extra caution
object_relations.object_representation: A more skilled, more reliable professional (needs to be relied on)

object_relations.self_representation: Someone who might potentially hurt others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking in counseling about needing to perform a lifting task or recalling a fall incident
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating inner Anxiety with objective danger, believing almost all lifting will cause accidents (transference: exaggerating risk into a certain threat)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Acknowledging concerns but constantly emphasizing risk and responsibility in interpretive language, in a cautious tone, focusing on facts and reasons, avoiding deep emotional experience.

manifestations: Experiences strong responsibility and moral pressure in volunteer work, worrying that their choices and actions will harm others
outcomes: Significant anxiety and avoidance behaviors, damaged confidence

manifestations: Relationship tension with other volunteers, feeling misunderstood; not talking to friends about Fear out of shame
outcomes: Reduced social support, shame and Anxiety maintained or worsened

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-doubt ('my training is not as good as others'), being overly cautious and self-limiting in lifting situations
Emphasizes 'it is all my responsibility', pays excessive attention to the possibility of mistakes

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Constraining myself with rule-like language: 'I should not lift them; professionals must do it'
Rigidly internalizes safety and professional standards as absolute requirements one must obey

positive_force: Previous experience and record of safely assisting residents
Positive attitude, willing to try behavioral experiments and homework practice
Able to identify and express automatic thoughts and trigger situations
Can obtain colleague support and assistance in the volunteer environment
negative_force: Catastrophizing and 'predicting the future' cognitive patterns reinforcing Fear
Strong attribution of responsibility to oneself and shame reduce the willingness to seek social support
Avoiding lifting tasks maintains and strengthens the Anxiety response
Belief in inadequate training weakening Self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Strong fear and avoidance of lifting or assisting the elderly
antecedent: Specific tasks at the nursing home requiring lifting or assisting
Recalling the witnessed fall from a few months ago
When realizing my training is not as good as some medical staff
target_behavior.core_reason: Generalizing risk and self-blaming after witnessing the fall, with catastrophizing and 'predicting the future' cognition; Increasing worry about inadequate training and Anticipation of mistakes.
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential danger and responsibility to reduce immediate Anxiety, while gaining brief security by seeking colleagues' comfort / having them take over
target_behavior.consequence: Volunteer ability affected, Relationship tension; marked physiological Anxiety in lifting situations (racing heart, sweating), reduced engagement in other activities
